key_insight: Open-weight large language models could extract key clinical findings from Finnish pediatric records with strong accuracy, and their uncertainty could flag likely mistakes for expert review.
clinical_relevance: This suggests hospitals may be able to reduce manual chart review by using uncertainty-based triage while still maintaining high-quality extraction from non-English EHRs.
method: Retrospective study of 97 Finnish pediatric ischemic stroke cases with four extraction targets.
Three open LLMs were run 15 times per task using multiple temperatures and repeats.
Shannon entropy and inter-model disagreement were used to rank cases for selective human review.
evidence_signal: Against clinician reference labels, gpt-oss-20b achieved F1 0.89-0.95 for non-control targets, and misclassified cases showed 2.4-3.4 times higher entropy; external validation in 88 neonatal stroke cases reached F1 0.95 for Apgar and binary seizure.
watch_item: Results come from a small, single-center retrospective cohort, so real-world performance and workflow impact may differ across hospitals, languages, and documentation styles.
paper_title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
